name: Common Scab (Streptomyces scabies)
symptoms: Raised, corky, rough lesions or pitted surface spots on potato skin affecting commercial appearance.
source: FSSAI Agricultural Quality Manual - Potato Section 4.2

name: Blackspot Bruising
symptoms: Internal grey or black discoloration beneath intact skin resulting from rough handling or mechanical drops during harvest.

name: Dry Rot (Fusarium spp.)
symptoms: Sunken, shriveled, dark brown to black surface lesions with internal cavities and white or pink fungal mycelium.

name: Bacterial Soft Rot (Pectobacterium carotovorum)
symptoms: Water-soaked, cream to tan colored soft macerated pulp with characteristic foul odor, spreading rapidly in warm storage.

name: Bacterial Brown Rot / Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum)
symptoms: Browning of vascular ring in tuber with bacterial slime oozing upon cross-section pressure.
source: Central Potato Research Institute Bacterial Wilt Guide

name: Blackleg (Dickeya & Pectobacterium)
symptoms: Inky black rotting starting from the stolon end progressing inwards into tuber flesh.

name: Black Scurf (Rhizoctonia solani)
symptoms: Hard, superficial, irregular dark brown or black sclerotia adhering firmly to the tuber skin like dirt that does not wash off.

name: Pink Rot (Phytophthora erythroseptica)
symptoms: Rubber-textured tuber flesh turning distinctive salmon-pink color upon exposure to air within 15-20 minutes.

name: Healthy Premium Potato Standard
symptoms: Firm texture, smooth uniform golden skin, absence of rot, lesions, corky scabs, or deep blackspot bruising.
source: AGMARK Grade Specifications for Table Potatoes 2024

name: Miscellaneous Superficial Blemish
symptoms: Minor surface scuffing, slight skin russeting, or minor non-pathogenic skin discolorations.
